sătrăpes , sătraps , is, and sătră-pa , ae (plur. satrapae), m., = σατράπης [Persian; cf. Gesenius, under ],
I.a governor of a province, a viceroy among the Persians, a satrap; nom. satrapes, Nep. Paus. 1, 2; id. Alcib. 10, 3; Curt. 8, 4, 21: “satrapa,” Ter. Heaut. 3, 1, 43 ; Curt. 3, 13, 1; Amm. 18, 6, 20: “satraps,” Sid. Carm. 2, 78 ; Alcim. 6, 392.—Gen. satrapis, Nep. Lys. 4, 1.—Acc. satrapen, Nep. Con. 2, 1: “satrapam,” Curt. 3, 13, 1 .—Plur. nom. satrapae, Nep. Dat. 3, 1; id. Ages. 2, 2; Vulg. Dan. 6, 6: “satrapes,” App. Mund. 26 .—Gen. satraparum, Plin. 6, 26, 30, § 119.—Acc. satrapas, Sid. Carm. 9, 50; Vulg. Esth. 3, 12.—Dat. satrapis, Vulg. 1 Reg. 29, 6.—Abl. satrapibus, Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. 2, 21.—Hence, gen., a ruler: “satrapae Philistinorum,” Vulg. Jud. 3, 3 ; id. 2 Par. 9, 14.—Hence, satră-pĭa or satrăpēa , ae, f., = σατραπεια, the office or province of a satrap, a satrapy, Plin. 6, 20, 23, § 78; Curt. 5, 1, 44; 6, 2, 5.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
